title: THE POWER OF NO
mv: But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.
mvp: “But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.” Daniel 3:18
assignment: Remember real-life situations from your past where you said yes instead of no. List five reasons you found it difficult to say no (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: “No” is used to indicate the absence of something, to give a negative response, to express refusal or disagreement, etc. No could also mean a vote not in favour of something/someone. Power means ability, physical force, strength, influence, etc. The Power 0f No is the ability to reject what is not good for us. It is the strength to disagree with a negative influence that may cause havoc to our lives or our relationship with God. You can say no to what is not good for you.
The following Bible characters said ‘no’ in diverse ways. Let us learn from them.

i: Joseph: He fled from sin by saying ‘no’ to the sexual advances of Potiphar’s wife (Genesis 39:11-12).
Paul: He kept his body under subjection and did not allow his flesh to rule over his spirit so as not to miss the ultimate crown of eternal life (1 Corinthians 9:26-27).
Ezra: He declined to go back on his word to the king that God would help them on their journey (Ezra 8:21-23).

Gideon: During the battle against the kings of Midian, Gideon and his men said ‘No’ to weariness until their enemies were destroyed. Although they were faint, they pursued their enemies and got the victory (Judges 8:4).
Jesus: He vehemently said ‘no’ to Satan’s temptations (Matthew 4:6-7).

b.x: The power to say no to any negativity is possible because humans are choice creatures with the willpower to make planned selections. We can say no to sin (Romans 6:12-14), temptation (1Corinthians 10:13; Matthew 26:41), negative influences (1 Peter 5:8-9), fears and doubts (Isaiah 41:10, James 1:6), worldly pleasures (James 4:4; 1 John 2:15-16), denial of faith (2 Timothy 2:12; Matthew 10:32-33), evil company (Proverbs 1:10), bitterness (Hebrews 12:15), laziness (Proverbs 18:9; 21:25), gluttony (Proverbs 23:20-21), past achievements (Philippians 3:13-14) and prayerlessness and lack of the study of God’s word (Psalm 119:147-148).

Saying no to frivolities helps us to affirm our person as a unique individual, and increases our confidence and trust in God (Nehemiah 2:20). It also creates safe and healthy boundaries, guides and helps us prioritise as we separate our needs from our wants, keeps us focused, helps us to be stable and free from needless pressure of satisfying human beings and being men-pleasers. It also brings delayed gratification.
Every yes to something meaningless is no to something meaningful. Your greatest ability is to say no when you need to.

i: Identify five people who said “No” in the Bible.
State at least five things believers are expected to say no to.
